anti_overlap: Does not cover the mathematical CPT composition or multiplier semantics — that is fd-conditional-probability-table-design.
Does not cover the Zod schema or YAML pipeline — that is fd-zod-yaml-schema-evolution.
Does not cover the political-science source citation fidelity of specific bias cells — that is fd-political-science-cohort-encoding.
decision_lens: Does the bias-roll matrix produce an Unc axis-value distribution that is compatible with the porch feeder's reveal cadence — specifically: does the joint distribution over all 8 axes produce a recognizable mix of common-type, recognizable-but-unusual, and genuinely-rare Uncs at the rates the feeder UX was designed for?
focus: Unc Rancher v0 product canon compliance for the bias-roll matrix: whether the matrix design respects the anchor-template boundary (matrix outputs axis values; solwend-6te consumes them — the matrix does not weight anchor templates directly), whether the matrix is compatible with the porch ledger's bird-feeder reframe (Uncs are revealed at the porch as reward, not browsed), and whether the matrix's output distribution produces the right mix of common / uncommon / rare-tier Uncs for the encounter density that the porch feeder UX was designed around.
name: fd-uncworld-anchor-boundary-coherence
persona: Apply the perspective of a product canon reviewer for Unc Rancher v0 who knows the PRD §9 bird-feeder reframe, the axis-vocabulary lock ground rules (grain coherence, orthogonality, legibility), the anchor-template boundary defined by solwend-6te, and the porch encounter mechanic (Uncs revealed as reward for completing a walk to a lure) — they care about whether the matrix's output distribution produces an Unc population that supports the bird-feeder reveal cadence without generating too many rare-tier Uncs (which breaks the reward-rarity gradient) or too many common-tier Uncs (which makes the porch boring), and flag any matrix design choice that bleeds across the anchor-template boundary or requires the engine to know about anchor types before rolling axis values.
review_areas: Anchor-template boundary enforcement: the brainstorm explicitly states 'Matrix outputs axis values; anchor templates match those values to type-templates. The matrix does NOT do anchor-level probability weighting.' Assess whether any of the 9 bias families' design descriptions could be misread as requiring the matrix to know which anchor templates exist — for example, if a bias family is described as 'bias toward anchor-types that are more common for working-class Uncs,' the matrix is implicitly doing anchor-level weighting. The matrix must be evaluable from axis values alone. This boundary is both a product-design choice and an architectural firewall: if solwend-1ke bleeds into solwend-6te's responsibility, future anchor-template additions require matrix changes.

Rarity-tier distribution: the PRD §9 bird-feeder reframe and encounter density design imply a frequency-of-appearance gradient where common-tier Uncs (high prior probability axis combinations) appear frequently, uncommon-tier Uncs appear occasionally, and rare-tier Uncs are genuine surprises. The bias-roll matrix, by elevating cross-axis multipliers for specific combination cells, effectively defines which axis combinations are rare. Assess whether the 9 bias families' design produces a joint distribution where the rare-tier Uncs (e.g., `tech-money × appalachian × single-anchor × Vietnam-era`) appear at a rate consistent with the feeder UX's surprise mechanic — or whether the matrix over-generates rare-cell combinations by having too many bias rules that concentrate probability mass in specific cells.

Dignity-rule compliance at the matrix level: the politics-axis flux-review locked the dignity rule as a primary constraint on value naming and description. The bias-roll matrix applies these values in cross-product combinations that the individual-value design did not anticipate. Assess whether any bias cell — a specific `when/then` combination — implicitly encodes a judgment about which Unc types are realistic or dignified. For example: if the matrix has a very high multiplier for `tech-money × traditionally-loyal → politics: single-anchor` (implying that wealthy-and-loyal Uncs are characteristically single-issue voters) while also having a low multiplier for `working-class × traditionally-loyal → politics: single-anchor` (implying that working-class loyal Uncs are not single-issue voters), the matrix is encoding a class-based political psychology judgment that the dignity rule should flag.

Bird-feeder reframe compatibility: in the PRD §9 bird-feeder model, the Unc is revealed at the porch as a reward after the walker completes a route to a lure. The walker does not browse or filter Uncs before seeing them. This means the matrix's output distribution must be coherent from the Unc's axis values alone — the porch feeder cannot reroll for a 'better' Unc or filter out Uncs the walker won't like. Assess whether the matrix design includes any mechanism that would require the feeder to inspect the rolled Unc's axis values and decide whether to present it — for example, if the matrix can produce an axis combination for which no anchor template exists (solwend-6te has no template for `finance-money × dissenting × platform-era`), the feeder will encounter a null-template failure. The matrix must guarantee that every possible axis-value combination has at least one valid anchor template in solwend-6te — or the matrix must constrain its output to only combinations that solwend-6te covers.

Modal-trajectory compatibility with porch encounter frequency: the Jennings-Niemi modal-trajectory finding (50%+ no-change political trajectory) implies that most Uncs will have `politics_formative = politics_current` — they were formed in one political posture and stayed there. If the porch encounter cadence is designed around the assumption that Uncs will be varied in type across encounters, a 50%+ same-posture rate means that consecutive porch Uncs may often have the same politics-posture value even if all other axes vary. Assess whether the matrix's modal-trajectory encoding interacts poorly with the encounter-density design — for example, if the encounter engine does not track recently-seen Uncs and avoid repeating politics-posture, a player who walks five routes in succession may see five `traditionally-loyal` Uncs in a row.

v1+ dignity-damping fields: the brainstorm specifies that `dissenting` (2-3%) and `convicted` (8%) carry hard rate-caps as v0 floors, with dynamic damping deferred to v1+. The v0 implementation has no cooldown mechanism. Assess whether the 2-3% and 8% floors are low enough to avoid the over-generation problem without cooldown — specifically, for a player who walks 20 routes in a week, how often will they encounter a `dissenting` or `convicted` Unc? If the floor rates produce noticeable over-generation at realistic walk frequencies (e.g., 1-2 walks/day × 7 days = 7-14 Uncs/week, of which 0-1 should be `dissenting` and 0-1 should be `convicted`), the v0 floor rates must be lower than 2-3% and 8% respectively.

severity_examples.condition: If the bias-roll matrix produces valid axis-value combinations that solwend-6te's anchor-template coverage does not include — for example, `finance-money × dissenting × platform-era × latin-america` — the porch feeder encounters a null-template at reveal time and must either show an error, skip the Unc, or fall back to a generic template. The brainstorm does not address this coverage gap. The matrix must either enumerate only axis combinations that solwend-6te covers (over-constraining the matrix) or solwend-6te must guarantee full coverage of all axis-value combinations (requiring coordination between solwend-1ke and solwend-6te).
severity_examples.scenario: The matrix can produce axis combinations for which solwend-6te has no anchor template, causing a null-template failure at porch reveal

severity_examples.condition: If the matrix's bias rules produce a materially higher probability of `politics: single-anchor` for `working-class` Uncs than for `professional` or `academic` Uncs with otherwise identical axis values, the matrix is encoding the political-science stereotype that working-class voters are single-issue voters while credentialed voters are multi-issue voters — a dignity violation that the axis-vocabulary lock's dignity rule explicitly prohibits. The dignity audit must extend to cross-axis probability distributions, not just individual value names.
severity_examples.scenario: The bias matrix encodes a dignity-violating class asymmetry in single-issue-coded probability

severity_examples.condition: If `traditionally-loyal` is the modal politics-posture (35-40% marginal) and the modal trajectory is no-change (50%+), then for a `traditionally-loyal` Unc, the probability of the next porch Unc also being `traditionally-loyal` is approximately 35-40% independent of the previous one. At 7 porch encounters per week, the expected number of `traditionally-loyal` encounters is 2-3 — which may feel repetitive. Without a v0 cooldown mechanism, the matrix's marginal rates must be calibrated against realistic encounter frequency to avoid perceptible type-clustering.
severity_examples.scenario: Modal-trajectory encoding produces consecutive same-politics Uncs at porch without cooldown, reducing feeder variety

success_hints: Before authoring bias rules for the 9 families, enumerate the set of axis-value combinations that solwend-6te's anchor templates cover. Any combination the matrix can produce but solwend-6te does not cover is a P0 gap. Resolve either by constraining the matrix (adding zero-weight bias rules for uncovered combinations) or by expanding solwend-6te's template coverage.

Apply the dignity-rule distribution audit: for each politics-posture value, compute the implied marginal probability conditional on class (summing over all other axes at their marginal rates). If any class × politics-posture conditional probability diverges from the overall marginal by more than 2x in either direction, flag it for a dignity review to assess whether the asymmetry is empirically warranted or encodes a class-based political psychology judgment.

Simulate the porch encounter cadence at 1-2 walks/day for 7 days against the matrix's implied joint distribution. Compute the expected counts of each politics-posture value over 7-14 encounters and check whether the variety is acceptable — and whether `dissenting` and `convicted` floor rates produce 0-1 encounters per week as intended.
task_context: Reviewing the brainstorm document for the Unc Rancher bias-roll matrix — specifically its compatibility with the v0 product canon (bird-feeder reframe, anchor-template boundary, porch encounter cadence, dignity rule at the distribution level) — to identify design choices that violate the anchor-template boundary, produce dignity-violating cross-axis distributions, or generate Unc populations incompatible with the feeder UX's rarity gradient and encounter frequency.
